name: tier0_mixed_distribution
_comment: THE FAIR SCENE, per LOOP-PROCESS §2.2 and the sighted round's brief: a mixed capture
matching the game's real distribution, not its worst corner alone.
WHY IT EXISTS. wall_face_review.json is a corridor with two crossings; corridor_junction is
a corridor with one. Both are corridor scenes, and under §3 a wall shows a front face only
where floor lies to its SOUTH, so a one-wide north-south corridor shows almost none. Eight
blind rounds answered 'is there thickness' with no, and most of those verdicts were taken on
scenes that could barely put a face in frame. That is the worst corner, judged alone.
The grammar must work everywhere, but it is judged on the distribution it ships in. So this
scene carries all three cases at once:
1. A ROOM WITH SOUTH-FACING REVEALS. Room A is 7x6 at x5-11, y4-9. Its north wall row
(y=3) is seven consecutive cells that each have floor to their south - seven true
front faces, in one span, inside the lit radius.
2. CORNERS. Room A's four outer corners, and the two inner corners where the chokepoint
leaves its south wall at (7,10) and (9,10).
3. A ONE-WIDE N-S CHOKEPOINT. x=8, y10-15. No cell in it has floor to its south, so it
shows no face at all - the §3 limit, present and unhidden. §8.2.1 keeps the chokepoint
in the game as a load-bearing roguelike verb; a scene that omits it is flattering.
Room B at the bottom sits outside the lit radius on purpose: the light arc (§6.2) is part
of the distribution too, and a scene where everything is lit is not the game.
THE PLAYER STANDS AT (8,6), INSIDE ROOM A. From there the north wall's face row is 3 tiles
away, room A's lit corners are 5, and the chokepoint mouth is 4 - all inside the 5.5-tile
radius the harness config carries. A scene whose subject sits outside the light tests
nothing, and that trap is recorded on corridor_junction.json already.
NEITHER EXISTING SPEC IS REPLACED. Both are cited by evidence already on disk and a swap
would silently invalidate those comparisons. This is a third spec, selected per capture.
